problem: Standard PointNav agents assume an idealized noise-free GPS+Compass sensor and deterministic actuation, which trivializes localization and does not match real robots. Agents without localization or under noisy actuation perform very poorly.
motivation: Real indoor robots have no perfect localization, and wheels slip and collide, so removing these assumptions is a step toward sim2real deployment. Monolithic end-to-end policies do not learn to integrate egomotion well. Separating dynamics (odometry) from the navigation policy could allow adapting to new dynamics without retraining the costly policy.
key_idea: Replace the oracle GPS+Compass with a frozen learned depth-based visual odometry CNN whose per-step egomotion estimates are integrated to update the relative goal coordinates fed to a DD-PPO policy.
insight: An explicit odometry module beats implicit learning: no-localization and auxiliary-loss agents reach SPL 0.096/0.179/0.086 versus 0.508 for ego-localization (noiseless). Learned odometry also beats dead-reckoning (SPL 0.303) because collisions break the fixed action-to-motion mapping. Decoupling allows hot-swapping: fine-tuning only the odometer for noisy actuation raises SoftSPL from 0.280 to 0.494 with a frozen policy. Locally accurate egomotion still accumulates drift over trajectories, causing premature stops (SoftSPL 0.813 vs SPL 0.508).
method: Visual odometry CNN: takes a concatenated pair of consecutive depth maps, passes them through 3 conv layers (8x8, 4x4, 3x3) and FC layers to a 512-d embedding, and regresses (dx,dy,dz,dtheta) with smooth-L1 loss; pre-trained then frozen.

Egomotion dataset: unroll a GPS-trained PointNav agent, sample 1000 (src,tgt) pairs per scene from 72 Gibson training scenes (72k pairs), and take ground-truth relative pose from simulator 6-DoF poses; a separate dataset is collected under noisy actuation.

Egomotion integration: convert each predicted egomotion to a 4x4 transform and apply it to the previous step's relative goal coordinates to obtain the current goal vector for the policy; the goal is given only once at episode start.
Noisy actuation model: LoCoBot-ILQR-derived Gaussian noise (bivariate on z/x, univariate on heading) with truncated sampling, added to every move-forward/turn action.

Policy training: 2-layer LSTM policy over ResNet-50 visual features, previous action and estimated goal, trained with DD-PPO for 60M frames (reward: success 1.0 + shaping - 0.01 slack), with encoder initialized from a 2.5B-frame GT-localization agent.

Hot-swapping adaptation: for noisy actuation, fine-tune only the odometer on the noisy dataset while keeping the policy frozen (retrained-odom), optionally also retraining the policy (retrained-odom+policy).
SoftSPL metric: replaces the binary success term of SPL with progress toward the goal (1 - dT/dinit) to give credit to failed but reasonable episodes.

setting.backbone: ResNet-50 + 2-layer LSTM policy (DD-PPO, trained with RL) + 3-layer CNN visual odometry model (supervised, frozen)
setting.training_data: Odometer: 72k depth pairs with GT egomotion from 72 Gibson train scenes (noiseless and noisy versions). Policy: DD-PPO for 60M frames in Gibson (8784 episodes, 72 scenes), encoder initialized from a 2.5B-frame GT-localization agent.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (depth used for odometry), goal given as relative coordinates only at start; no GPS+Compass
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT pose used only for training the odometer)

numbers_note: The Gibson val numbers are on 994 episodes across 14 scenes; the 300M-frame noisy results (ego-localization SoftSPL=0.517, SPL=0.034, geo d T=2.535) appear only in the appendix text.
results: Without GPS+Compass and with noiseless actuation, ego-localization reaches SPL 0.508 / SoftSPL 0.813, beating dead-reckoning (SPL 0.303) and no-localization (SPL 0.096). Under noisy actuation, retrained odometer+policy gets SoftSPL 0.576 versus 0.515 for no-localization and 0.407 for dead-reckoning. The classic ORB-SLAM2 pipeline has higher noisy-setting success (SPL 0.267, Succ 0.700) but far lower SoftSPL (0.301). A modified version ranked #1 on SoftSPL and distance to goal in Habitat Challenge 2020 PointNav.
limitations: Integrated odometry drift causes premature stop calls, so SPL/success remains far below the GT-localization oracle (0.508 vs 0.866 SPL).
In the noisy setting, absolute SPL/success remain very low (SPL 0.047), and the classic pipeline has higher success there.
Evaluated only in simulation with simulated noise (LoCoBot noise models), with no real-robot experiments; the odometer relies on depth and needed a ResNet18 encoder under sensor noise.
